common_name: Black Beauty Heuchera (Glossy Black-Red Ruffled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil, setting the crown at or slightly above grade since heuchera rot if buried too deep.

directions: Site Black Beauty in partial shade to full sun, giving it a few hours of protection from the hottest afternoon sun in warm climates to keep its color from bleaching. Its glossy, ruffled leaves emerge nearly black with a ruby-red backlit glow when sunlight passes through them, one of the darkest and shiniest leaf colors among coral bells, and the foliage holds that color through the growing season rather than fading to green. Airy, wiry flower stems carry small white blooms above the foliage in late spring, drawing hummingbirds and other pollinators. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor and foliage color.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil; this selection tolerates more sun than many coral bells once established.

directions: Rosewood performs well in both full sun and part shade, making it a flexible choice for mixed borders and containers where light conditions vary through the season. Its compact mound of glossy, wavy-edged foliage emerges a deep burnt-umber brown and keeps that warm color consistently through summer heat. In late spring, feathery plumes of cream-colored flowers rise above the foliage on slender stems, larger than the blooms of many other coral bells and attractive to hummingbirds. Keep soil evenly moist but well drained, and divide clumps every few years once the center begins to thin.

common_name: Shanghai Heuchera (Silvery-Purple CITY Series Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Part of Terra Nova's CITY series, Shanghai forms a tidy, clump-forming evergreen mound of dramatic silvery-purple foliage that holds its color from spring through fall. From late spring into fall, panicles of small white bell-shaped flowers rise on slender stems well above the leaves and repeat-bloom through the season, a trait shared by the other CITY-series selections. The dense habit resists flopping and keeps the silvery leaf color facing upward for best display. Grow in partial shade with consistent moisture for the richest foliage color and longest bloom.

common_name: Tokyo Heuchera (Lime-Green CITY Series Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Tokyo, another member of Terra Nova's CITY series, spreads into a low, wide mound of lime-green leaves that brightens shaded plantings without the need for variegation. Short spikes of red flowers appear over the foliage in summer, from July into September, giving a longer and later bloom window than many spring-flowering coral bells. Grow in partial shade with evenly moist, well-drained soil; too much hot afternoon sun can scorch the chartreuse foliage. Combine with purple- or burgundy-leaved companions for strong color contrast in a shaded border.

common_name: Testarossa Heuchera (Bright Red Mounding Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in moderately well-drained, organically rich soil; tolerates more sun than most coral bells.

directions: Named for the Italian word for 'redhead,' Testarossa forms a stout, full mound of large, leathery, bright red leaves on short petioles, giving the plant fullness without the stemmy look of some red heucheras. The vivid red color holds especially well into fall, making it a strong accent for mass plantings, edging, and borders. White flowers appear over an unusually long season from late spring into late summer. Testarossa tolerates full sun to part shade, heat, drought, and poor soil better than many ornamental coral bells, making it a reliable choice for sunnier mixed beds.

common_name: Zipper Heuchera (Color-Changing Ruffled Villosa-Type Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained soil; villosa-type parentage gives it better heat tolerance than many coral bells.

directions: A 2015 Terra Nova introduction, Zipper combines the summer-heat tolerance of Heuchera villosa with the heavy leaf ruffling typical of cold-hardy coral bells. Its compact clump of intensely ruffled leaves emerges burgundy and gradually becomes suffused with orange, shifting seasonally from orange tones in spring and fall to golden amber in summer and winter, always showing magenta undersides along the ruffled edges. Grow in partial shade with good drainage; this villosa heritage makes Zipper more forgiving of summer humidity and heat than many purely americana-type selections. Divide every three to four years to keep the color display fresh.

common_name: Red Lightning Heuchera (Gold-Leaf Red-Veined Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil; gold leaf color is brightest with some morning sun.

directions: Red Lightning carries large gold leaves traced with electrifying dark red veins, a striking two-tone pattern that holds its contrast through most of the growing season rather than fading as summer progresses. Sprays of small white flowers appear over the foliage in summer on wiry stems that draw pollinators and hummingbirds. Grow in partial shade with some morning sun for the brightest gold color; too much shade can mute the contrast between the gold blade and red veining. Well-drained, humus-rich soil and regular moisture keep the foliage lush through the season.

common_name: Ruby Tuesday Heuchera (Silver-Frosted Ruby-Red Ruffled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Ruby Tuesday forms a low, leathery mound of extremely ruffled leaves that emerge a clear ruby red and age into a deep merlot tone frosted lightly with silver along the folds. Small white blossoms appear over the foliage in late spring, drawing bees and hummingbirds to the garden. The dense ruffling catches light attractively and gives the clump a textured, almost sculptural look even without flowers. Grow in partial shade with evenly moist, well-drained soil, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain tight, colorful foliage.

common_name: Peppermint Spice Heuchera (Rose-Pink Flowered Green Spice Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Peppermint Spice shares the marbled, silver-veined green foliage pattern of the popular 'Green Spice' coral bells, but pairs it with rose-pink flowers held on medium-height stems in a cross combining Green Spice-type foliage with H. sanguinea-type bloom color. Flower stems reach well above the compact 8-inch foliage mound, giving a long season of color from late spring into summer. The patterned leaves provide ornamental interest even when not in bloom, with silvery overlay tracing the veins against a green background that deepens with cooler fall temperatures. Grow in partial shade with evenly moist, well-drained soil for the best leaf pattern and flower display.

common_name: Peach Smoothie Heuchera (Blended Peach-Orange Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Peach Smoothie produces a smooth blend of peach and soft orange tones across its ruffled foliage, a gentler, more pastel take on Terra Nova's warm-colored coral bells lineup. The color deepens and warms slightly as the season progresses, holding interest from spring through fall without the need for flowers. Airy stems of small white blooms rise above the foliage in late spring and draw pollinators to the garden. Grow in partial shade with consistent moisture and good drainage, and divide every few years once the clump center begins to decline.

common_name: FOREVER Midnight Heuchera (Opalescent Purple-Black Ruffled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil; tolerates full sun to full shade once established.

directions: Part of Terra Nova's FOREVER collection, Midnight carries deep purple-black leaves with crisp, heavily ruffled edges and an opalescent sheen that shifts through shades of amethyst, violet, and plum as light hits it from different angles. Delicate white flowers appear from late spring through much of summer, attracting hummingbirds and other pollinators over an unusually long bloom window. The FOREVER series is bred for exceptional heat and sun tolerance, and Midnight holds its dark color and ruffled texture across a wide range of exposures from full shade to full sun. Use it as an edger, border plant, or container specimen in well-drained, humus-rich soil.

common_name: GRANDE Black Heuchera (Oversized Wavy Burgundy-Black Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil; give extra spacing for its oversized mature footprint.

directions: GRANDE 'Black' is bred for scale, carrying large, wavy, dark burgundy-to-black leaves on a bold mound far bigger than a typical coral bells clump, making a strong landscape or large-container statement. The neat, mounded habit tolerates summer heat and humidity better than many dark-leaved selections, and in summer it sends up airy tufts of tiny pink flowers that contrast nicely with the nearly black foliage. Grow in partial shade to full sun in well-drained, humus-rich soil, allowing generous spacing since this series grows considerably larger than standard heuchera. Divide only when the clump becomes congested, since GRANDE selections are slower to need division than compact types.

common_name: GRANDE Carnelian Heuchera (Oversized Ruffled Copper-Red Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil; give extra spacing for its oversized mature footprint.

directions: A new-for-2026 addition to Terra Nova's GRANDE series, Carnelian is bred for oversized, ruffled leaves in a rich carnelian red brightened by coppery undertones. Its flower stems rise to about thirty inches, well above the eighteen-inch foliage mound, giving it presence toward the back of a shaded border or as a specimen in a large container. Like other GRANDE selections, Carnelian grows considerably larger than standard coral bells, so allow generous spacing when planting. Grow in partial shade to full sun in well-drained, humus-rich soil with regular moisture for the fullest leaf color.

common_name: DOLCE Glazed and Infused Heuchera (Silver Leaf Charcoal-Veined Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained soil; site in filtered sun or shade in hot southern climates.

directions: A 2026 addition to the Walters Gardens DOLCE line, Glazed and Infused carries large silver leaves etched with charcoal-black veins and a gentle ruffle along the margins. It forms a dense, mounding habit that performs from full sun to shade, and in early summer sends up upright scapes of deep rose-pink flowers over an unusually long bloom period. The silvery foliage brightens shaded plantings and container combinations, and its compact size suits edging and small-space gardens. Grow in well-drained soil and provide protection from the hottest afternoon sun in warm southern zones to keep the silver color crisp.

common_name: DOLCE Sultry Night Heuchera (Glossy Black Purple-Overlay Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade.

directions: Sultry Night is a dense, rounded DOLCE-series selection with ruffled black foliage washed in a purple overlay that matches the purple undersides of its leaves and stems. New growth emerges glossy in spring and holds its deep, rich tone through the entire season rather than fading in summer heat. Short petioles keep the habit tight and compact, reaching only about ten inches tall, making it well suited to containers and small-space edging. Grow in partial shade with evenly moist, well-drained soil, and pair with silver- or gold-leaved companions for strong contrast.
